newsitem.title: USA: RockShox sees record sales, profits in '98.
newsitem.headline: RockShox sees record sales, profits in '98.

text.p: RockShox Inc said Monday it expects record sales and profits in fiscal 1998 but a slower rate than in 1997.
"We recognize that there is softness in the domestic mountain bike market and are accordingly taking a conservative outlook for the balance of the year," said Steve Simons, chairman and president.

"However, with our new products, the international scope of our business, and our continuing success in developing and implementing manufacturing and operating efficiencies, we believe that fiscal 1998 should be another year of record sales and profits, but at a slower growth rate than last year," Simons said in a statement.

RockShox Monday reported fiscal 1998 first quarter net income of $2.9 million, or $0.21 a share, on revenues of $24.7 compared with profits of $1.3 million, or $0.14 a share, on revenues of $21.4 million for the comparable year-ago period.
